a_true, b_true = 0.20, 0.15   # seconds, seconds/bit — typical mouse values
distances = [64, 128, 256, 512]   # px
widths = [8, 24, 64]              # px
TRIALS = 15

rows = []
for D in distances:
    for W in widths:
        ID = np.log2(D / W + 1)
        mt = a_true + b_true * ID + rng.normal(0, 0.04, TRIALS)
        for m in mt:
            rows.append((D, W, ID, max(m, 0.05)))

data = np.array(rows)  # columns: D, W, ID, MT
print(f"{len(data)} pointing trials, ID range "
      f"{data[:,2].min():.2f}-{data[:,2].max():.2f} bits")
description: You can follow distance-width combinations into a four-column dataset.

steps.description: You define model coefficients, four distances and three widths. TRIALS requests 15 observations for each distance-width pair.
The nested loops compute ID as log2(D / W + 1). You generate a noisy modeled sample for the current pair.
